#+TITLE: bisos_deb13-sysd-2 --- Second Instance of bisos_deb13-sysd
#+OPTIONS: toc:nil

This leaf of [[https://github.com/bxObjects/bro_dockerfiles][bro_dockerfiles]] runs a *second instance*
of the =bisos_deb13-sysd= image (Debian 13, systemd as PID 1, an XFCE desktop over VNC and noVNC,
sshd; a *privileged* docker container), next to the first instance of =../bisos_deb13-sysd=.

* A Numeric Suffix Means a Shared Image

A leaf named =<primary>-<N>= is instance =N= of the image of =../<primary>=. It has no image of its
own. Here:

- *Shared:* the image =bisos_deb13-sysd:latest=. It is built only in =../bisos_deb13-sysd=.
  =./imageBuild.sh= here builds nothing: it says so and prints the command for the primary leaf.
- *Per instance:* the container name, the host ports and, on cgroup v1, the compose network and its
  subnet. These must stay distinct from every other instance's, so that the instances run side by
  side and creating, stopping or deleting one never touches another.

| Leaf                 | Container            |  SSH |  VNC | noVNC | cgroup v1 subnet |
|----------------------+----------------------+------+------+-------+------------------|
| =bisos_deb13-sysd=   | =bisos_deb13-sysd=   | 2224 | 5903 |  6903 | =172.16.12.0/24= |
| =bisos_deb13-sysd-2= | =bisos_deb13-sysd-2= | 2227 | 5906 |  6906 | =172.16.13.0/24= |

The subnets are hand-picked today; a further instance must pick one that is free on the host and
distinct from these (=containerManage.sh create= refuses an overlapping one). Assigning them from a
registrar, with the ports, is planned in bisos.dockerProc (Stage 4 of its AI-WorkPlan.org).

Each container has its own writable layer, its own =tmpfs= mounts and its own =/shuttle/this= (this
leaf). Rebuilding the image in the primary leaf does not change a container that already exists:
it keeps the image it was created from until it is deleted and created again.

The =Dockerfile= and =dockerConf/= in this leaf are left from the copy this leaf started as. They are
not used: the compose files here have no =build:= section, and the image comes from the primary leaf.

* Files in This Leaf

| File                      | Purpose                                                         |
|---------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| =docker-compose.yml=      | How to run this instance on a *cgroup v2* host.                 |
| =docker-compose.cgv1.yml= | How to run this instance on a *cgroup v1* host.                 |
| =imageBuild.sh=           | Points at the primary leaf; builds nothing here.                |
| =containerManage.sh=      | Standalone: create, start, stop, restart, delete this instance. |
| =verify.sh=               | Standalone: smoke-test this running instance.                   |
| =dockerProc.spcs=         | With BISOS: the planted =bisos.dockerProc= command (see below). |

=imageBuild.sh= and =containerManage.sh= are the same files as in the primary leaf (and in every
leaf of bro_dockerfiles). Everything that differs between instances is in the compose files.

** The two compose files

A container with systemd as PID 1 needs the host's cgroup hierarchy, and that differs between cgroup
versions, so there is one compose file for each:

- =docker-compose.yml= (cgroup v2): =cgroup: host= and =/sys/fs/cgroup= mounted read-write.
- =docker-compose.cgv1.yml= (cgroup v1): no =cgroup: host=; =/sys/fs/cgroup= mounted read-only with
  only its =systemd= subtree read-write. It gives the container its own bridge network,
  =bisos_deb13_sysd2_cgv1=, on the explicit subnet =172.16.13.0/24=.

You do not pick one: =containerManage.sh= reads the host's cgroup version and uses the matching file.

* Standalone Usage

Requirements: docker, and compose --- either the =docker compose= plugin or the older =docker-compose=
binary. Both scripts refuse to run inside a container: run them on the host, from any directory.

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
./containerManage.sh [-n] <create|start|stop|restart|delete|status>
#+END_SRC

| Verb          | Does                                                         | Compose command            |
|---------------+--------------------------------------------------------------+----------------------------|
| =create=      | Create the container, not started.                           | =up --no-start --no-build= |
| =start=       | Start it.                                                    | =start=                    |
| =stop=        | Stop it. The container and its writable layer are kept.      | =stop=                     |
| =restart=     | Stop then start it.                                          | =restart=                  |
| =delete=      | Remove container + network. Writable layer lost, image kept. | =down=                     |
| =status=      | Show cgroup version, compose file, state and host ports.     | =ps=                       |
| =vncPassword= | =set= or =clear= the VNC password (see below).               | =cp=, =restart=            |

Before =create=, the script checks, and if any check fails reports every problem and creates nothing:
- the container does not already exist;
- none of its host ports is in use;
- on cgroup v1, the compose network's subnet overlaps no other docker network and no host route
  (the host's own interface subnets included);
- the shared image has been built (if not, it prints the command for the primary leaf).

=-n= is a dry run: the checks still run, but the commands that would change anything are printed,
not executed. =delete= runs =compose down= for this leaf's compose project only (compose names the
project after the leaf directory), so it removes this instance and its network, never the primary's.

A first run, after the primary leaf has built the image:

#+BEGIN_SRC bash
( cd ../bisos_deb13-sysd && ./imageBuild.sh )      # the shared image, in the primary leaf
./containerManage.sh -n create
./containerManage.sh create
./containerManage.sh start
./verify.sh
#+END_SRC

** VNC password (optional)

VNC and noVNC have *no password by default*. =./containerManage.sh vncPassword set= gives this
instance one (it asks twice, and restarts the container if it runs); =vncPassword clear= goes back
to none; =status= shows "VNC auth: none | password". The password is kept in this instance's
container, independent of the primary's, and is lost on =delete=. Only its first 8 characters
count, and VNC traffic is not encrypted: across a network, use an SSH tunnel.

* Ports and Connecting

| Service | Host port | Container port | Connect with                          |
|---------+-----------+----------------+---------------------------------------|
| SSH     |      2227 |             22 | =ssh -p 2227 <user>@localhost=        |
| VNC     |      5906 |           5901 | a VNC client at =localhost:5906=      |
| noVNC   |      6906 |           6901 | a browser at =http://localhost:6906/= |

* Verifying: =verify.sh=

With the container running, =./verify.sh= (defaults: =bisos_deb13-sysd-2 2227 5906 6906=) checks that
systemd is PID 1, that the =vncserver=, =novnc= and =sshd-container= services are active, that
journald works, that the host ports listen and that noVNC answers over HTTP. It exits non-zero if any
check fails.

* With BISOS

=bisos.dockerProc= knows the numeric-suffix rule (since 2026-10-26): =./dockerProc.spcs= in this
leaf uses the image =bisos_deb13-sysd:latest= of the primary leaf, and this leaf's own container
name and host ports, read from its =docker-compose.yml=. =containerProc_imageBuild= builds
nothing here, and =containerProc_imageDelete= / =containerProc_fullClean= leave the shared image
alone. =bisos.dockerProc= supports cgroup v2 hosts only; on a cgroup v1 host its commands refuse
to run.
